title: Vu 3 ube (Leyte): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Vu 3 ube: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Vu 3 ube is an ube variety. About 8 months to harvest, 21.3 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Vu 3 is a registered ube variety, also sold or known as Leyte or Leyte ubi. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1988. It takes about 8 months from planting to harvest, with 21.26 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Leyte or Leyte ubi, this is the same ube. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [ube variety finder](/crop-varieties/ube), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 8 months from planting to harvest.
**Yield:** 21.26 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Vu 3 ube takes about 8 months from planting to harvest. That is about the average of the 8 ube varieties with a day count, 7.6 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 21.26 t/ha beats the average of its group, 16. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit ube fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have white flesh and brown with black tinge skin. The starch content is 20.93 percent.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Registry: white flesh, cream to pink cortex, brown skin with black tinge, described by UPLB as creamy pink.
Registered in 1988 with the Philippine Seed Board.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the highest yielding of the early ViSCA yams in the registry. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Vu 3 ube
Processors pay for a deep purple flesh that stays purple when cooked. Pick a registered variety for color and yield, and plant whole small tubers or setts.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Leyte the same as Vu 3?
items.a: Yes. Leyte is another name for Vu 3. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 8 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 21.26 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Vu 3?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
